limitations: Synthetic authored-expert jaw labels and privileged simulator sensing; not human video or hardware.
Only the jaw is controlled by the new learned adapter; all six arm commands remain the frozen v0.1 primitive.
Same rigid 40 g block, two trained destinations and narrow starting region as v0.1.
Development starts were reused after five full-residual candidates each failed all 16 development cases.
Interventions affect acquisition; airborne regrasp and general slip recovery are not established.
Native servos, joint/jaw caps and gravity compensation remain authored.
Timing excludes sensing, network transport and physical actuators; no hard real-time guarantee.

native_dataset.note: Exact dataset commit configured by a derived hosting patch; consult its publication receipt for public-tree checks and anonymous hosting-file readback.

replay_loading: Each replay has separate hash-bound frame metadata and pose chunks. The browser loads only the selected replay; chunks are at most 8 MiB.
scope: Recorded synthetic PiPER learned-grip simulation. Only the jaw adapter is newly learned; all six arm commands remain the frozen v0.1 learned primitive. Native model geometry and saved states reconstructed with mj_forward only; no browser physics, live policy, human-video learning or physical robot qualification. The blind control is a separately trained learner without live feedback, not a shuffled-label model.
selection_notice: All 24 feedback confirmation attempts are replayable, plus the first scheduled case of each blind, feedforward, teacher and open-jaw control. Selection never depends on outcome. All 120 attempts retain local 20 ms traces, scores and receipts. Original 1 ms numeric arrays are linked to the public dataset with their source hashes; they are not duplicated in this viewer projection.
